findings.claim_summary: Adapter signal: TypeORM migration surfaces show repeated boilerplate across services — at least three migrations follow the same add-column-then-index pattern with no shared helper

Plan 016 implementation arc shipped nine SHADOW adapter rows + four impact graph source stubs without operator-facing parser implementations and zero PR pipeline test coverage; the Plan 016 sign-off review recorded each of the three architectural debts but the DEBT records emitted in Plan 017 Phase 2 cite F-001 (TypeORM duplication) as their originating finding, which has no content link to any of the three debts.

Plan 016 implementation arc registered 9 adapters in aria-tools/registry.json and 4 impact graph sources in aria-kernel/aria_kernel/recursive_impact.py; as of HEAD 97fca751, 8 adapters still use the SHADOW shadow_runner.py and 3 sources still emit status: unknown stubs. Plan 019 Phase 4 + 5 + 9 close this finding by completing each parser implementation and each source mapping.

Plan 022 v6 sign-off (HEAD 6090b67b) declared kernel-correctness closure complete; post-push external audit identified 30 architectural bypass routes still reachable. Plan 023 v3 corrective-arc closed via 32 fix items across 7 tiers.

Plan 023 v3.1 sign-off (HEAD e4f3218e) closed 32 bypass routes from F-004 but a follow-up audit identified 15 architectural-quality gaps still alive: legacy submit CLI, creation API gap, workflow injection, runtime profile fail-open, validation matrix projection strip, snapshot adapter fallback + partial pre-merge, tool run CLI exit-0 + run_tool API contract, mock CI executor, claim_request non-atomic, submit no idempotency, malformed lease expiry, validate_response role match, evidence canonical (string + dict paths), spine status whitelist, JSONL silent-skip + governance recursion. Plan 024 v3 corrective-arc tracks closure via 16 fix items.

Operator-conducted ARIA self-audit (2026-05-10) identified two architectural-quality gaps in the kernel-internal silencing/tracking discipline: (1) pressure._phase2_effective_context wraps both the deferred trust import and the trust function calls in a single broad except, silently swallowing real data errors from trust functions feeding pressure evaluation feeding operator decisions; (2) cycle.py:54-56 documents pr_lifecycle phase as emitting a placeholder governance event but carries no aria-debt:DEBT-... source-side marker and no entry in aria-state/architectural_debt.jsonl, in violation of CONTRACTS.md §6.6 + IDENTITY.md §3.6 short-term-workaround-as-tracked-debt schema.
